Use the separable closure as the intermediate field consisting exactly of elements of the ambient field that are separable over the base.

- For the first conjunct, every element of \(L\) is separable over \(L\) (its minimal polynomial is linear). Hence \(L\) lies in \(\operatorname{separableClosure}(L,E)\); restricting scalars from \(L\) to \(F\) does not change this underlying inclusion.

- For the second conjunct, use the universal property of \(\operatorname{adjoin}_F(S)\). If the adjoin is a separable \(F\)-algebra, each generator \(x\in S\) is separable. Conversely, if every \(x\in S\) is separable over \(F\), then
  \[
  S\subseteq \operatorname{separableClosure}(F,E).
  \]
  Since the separable closure is an intermediate field, minimality of `IntermediateField.adjoin` gives
  \[
  \operatorname{adjoin}_F(S)\le \operatorname{separableClosure}(F,E).
  \]
  Thus every element of the adjoin is separable over \(F\), which is precisely `Algebra.IsSeparable F (adjoin F S)`.

The only bookkeeping is translating between elements of the intermediate-field subtype and their images in \(E\), plus the scalar-restriction coercion in the first conjunct.
